findings.text: Step 3 (measure before/after) was never done — there's no measurement file anywhere under `/framework/ai/2026-10-05/mobile-reload-speed/` (only `requirements.md`, `task.jsonl`, `files.jsonl`, `review/`), yet the landing commit (`eecf012a`, `Server/compress.js`) says "See public/framework/ai/2026-10-05/mobile-reload-speed/ for the before/after measurement." That line points at nothing. Either run the headless throttled-load measurement the requirements ask for (time to first paint/total, request count, 304 count) and add it to the task folder, or fix the commit message so it stops claiming proof that isn't there.

Reading the requirements heading literally — "Do (step 1 only; safe, no stale files)" — the work correctly did ETag/304 only and left modulepreload (step 2) out; that's the right call, since step 2 needs the owner's URL-versioning decision noted at the bottom as "not in scope." Worth saying explicitly in the landing report so the next reader doesn't think modulepreload was forgotten.

Server/compress.js:54 compares `If-None-Match` with plain `===` against compress.js's own mtime+size ETag string. If a client ever revalidates a URL that compress.js skips this time (e.g. a byte-range request, or Accept-Encoding missing) using an ETag it got from compress.js on a prior load, the request falls through to `express.static`, whose `send`-package ETag has a different format — the comparison always misses and the browser gets a full 200 instead of a 304. Rare in normal phone-reload use (browsers always send Accept-Encoding), not worth blocking on.

The change is not yet merged into `michael/dev` (still on `worktree/mobile-reload-speed`, commit `eecf012a`) — expected, since `merge.mjs` wants this review first. Once this lands, run `restart_server monorepo` per requirements step 4.
